intent: Trace the estimated supply of new certified teachers in the United States over the years from 2005 to 2017 and quantify the overall change.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the video trace the estimated supply of new certified teachers in the United States from 2005 to 2017 and quantify the overall change?
The estimated supply of new certified teachers decreased by 85,000 from 175,000 in 2005 to 90,000 in 2017, an overall decline of about 48.6%.

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The estimated supply of new certified teachers in the United States rose from 175,000 in 2005 to a peak of 195,000 in 2008, then declined to 90,000 by 2017.
units.computation: Sequence of values: 175000 (2005) -> 195000 (2008) -> 185000 (2009) -> 110000 (2013) -> 90000 (2017); direction changes from increasing to decreasing after 2008.
accept: Describes an initial increase to a peak around 2008 followed by a sustained decline through 2017.
Mentions the overall downward trajectory after the 2008 peak.
reject: Claims the supply increased monotonically from 2005 to 2017.
Omits the 2008 peak or the subsequent decline.

units.claim: The estimated supply of new certified teachers decreased by 85,000 from 175,000 in 2005 to 90,000 in 2017, an overall decline of about 48.6%.
accept: States the overall change from 2005 to 2017 as a decrease of 85,000.
States the overall percentage decline as approximately 48.6% (or about 49%).
reject: Reports an increase instead of a decrease.
Uses endpoints other than 2005 and 2017 for the overall change.

optional_valid: Mentions the intermediate value of 185,000 in 2009 or 110,000 in 2013 as part of the decline.
Notes that the maximum value in the period was 195,000 in 2008.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the decline (e.g., policy changes, economic conditions) not present in the table.
Claims about years or data points not listed in the table summary.
Comparisons with other countries or teacher supply categories not in the data.
review_notes: The table summary lists x_anchors including 2005, 2008, 2009, 2013, and 2017; point_order 5 is absent, so the sequence uses the provided rows only.
The trend unit combines the rise and fall into one overall trajectory because the intent asks to trace the series over the period.
The change unit quantifies the overall change using the first and last available points (2005 and 2017).
